patch.value: Split from PR 24 by orchestrator decision. Own all journaled recovery, native close ownership proof and multi-item compensation. Current PR only performs fresh native close and refuses replay without automatic repair.

Canonicalize short IDs through host native get before every history read, including service-capable contexts; capture history heads before authoritative decision documents and recheck under the same native writer lock; identify own forward close and every restore by a durable unique compensation_id and exact SDK journal identity, never author, message markers or document equality; refuse unrelated same-author native closes and copied transaction markers; native close owns dependent unblock, blocker-field removal, Plan behavior and unchanged warnings, and actual read-back defines successors; persist full immutable member/pre-close bytes digest/post-close history domain before restore, fsync intent, progress and parent-directory updates; durable per-member restored/pending receipts recover own progress without mistaking it for peers; never restore peers or foreign records, and release/claim/restore ABA must be detected from locked native history heads even when all bytes and tokens match; real-process SIGKILL after every forward and reverse step including 0..N member restores with 1-3 dependents converges to exact pre-close item bytes with append-only audit history, no duplicates or loss; peer edits between restores stop with typed partial receipts preserving restored and pending members; lost native returns and ordinary coordinator failures preserve all lifecycle members coherently; packed npm/Bun, non-Git and installed separate/shared SDK layouts exercise every boundary; property tests, revert proofs, full 100 percent coverage, documentation and release gates.

value.text: Pre-gate adversarial review found a real ownership gap: copying the global close episode onto an untouched admitted member could make a peer edit look like an owned forward mutation.
